Thanks Samir — great questions and really helpful context on egress/mTLS. Recap and immediate next steps below.

Recap (short):
- Supported connectivity models: Hosted API (public TLS with token auth), Dedicated (Redwood-managed GPUs with private control plane), and Private (customer-managed VPC with private control plane).
- For Dedicated: we offer VPC endpoints (private link style) so you don’t need outbound NAT; we also support egress configurations if you want the runtime to egress through your NAT/Gateway.
- IP allowlist: we can supply static egress IPs for Dedicated and ranges for Hosted; for Private deployments, control is on your side.
- mTLS: we support mTLS for our private control plane connections; for customer-initiated inbound requests we typically recommend using our VPC endpoint (no public IP) + mutual TLS for the control plane. We can do client certs for connections to the control plane.

Requested artifacts we will provide:
- Network architecture sketch (VPC endpoints, subnets, SGs)
- Integration checklist (SDK auth examples, required ports, DNS entries, cert rotation guidance)
- Sample code: embeddings -> reranker -> structured output example (Node + Python snippets)

Samir,

Attaching a first-draft architecture sketch in-line below and a short checklist. High level notes:

- Option A (recommended): Redwood Dedicated with VPC Endpoint
  - Your VPC creates an interface endpoint (or private link) to Redwood's dedicated subnet. Traffic never traverses the public internet.
  - Redwood terminates TLS; we support mutual TLS on the control plane for admin RPCs. For inference traffic we support mTLS if you need client certs — we will exchange CA and cert metadata and can automate rotation via our control plane.
  - DNS: use a private hosted zone that resolves the Redwood endpoint to the interface endpoint IPs. We provide suggested Route53 records (or zone file entries).

- Option B: Outbound egress to Redwood (less preferred for strict compliance)
  - Your infra NATs outbound requests to Redwood's public endpoints. We can provide static egress IP ranges for Dedicated customers to allowlist. Note that DNS resolution will be public.

Checklist (network):
- Open outbound TLS (443) to Redwood control plane for provisioning (if using our control plane).
- If using interface endpoint: provision subnets and SG rules to allow traffic from app servers to endpoint IPs.
- Provide cert signing request if you want mTLS for inference connections.
- Confirm whether you require TLS client cert validation at the inference layer or only at the control plane.

I attached a simple diagram (finpay-network-diagram.png). Happy to iterate.

-Jonas
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Aisha — quick answers inline: 

1) Endpoint IP stability: For interface endpoints the private IPs are assigned from your subnet(s) and are stable from your side; Redwood can provide a stable DNS name (private zone) that resolves to those IPs. For our egress IPs (if you use NAT outbound), we publish a small set of static ranges and communicate scheduled maintenance windows in advance.

2) Bring-your-own-CA (BYOCA): Yes — we support customer-managed CAs for mTLS. We'll coordinate CSR exchange and can document the rotation process in the checklist.

3) Sample flow (summary):
- Step 1 (Embedding): send /v1/embeddings with service token over mTLS. Payload: 5k text chars typically -> embedding vectors (1 request per doc).
- Step 2 (Candidate retrieval): your search service queries vector DB (local) to return top ~200 candidates.
- Step 3 (Rerank): batch candidates and send to Redwood's /v1/completions with structured input (system + tool call schema) to produce ordered results; payloads are predictable — typical request is ~50-200 tokens for ranking. We include a code sample in the attached snippets.

Attachments: small Node + Python snippets showing SDK auth header, token refresh, and batch embeddings + rerank pseudo-code. Will drop the detailed snippets to the Drive folder and paste a short Node example below.

Node snippet (very short):
const client = new Redwood({ endpoint: 'https://private.redwood.finpay.internal', mTLS: { cert: 'path/to/cert.pem', key: 'path/to/key.pem' } });
const emb = await client.embeddings.create({ model: 'rw-embed-1', input: docs });
// local vector search -> candidates
const rerank = await client.completions.create({ model: 'rw-rerank-1', input: { prompt: 'Rerank these candidates', candidates } });
